title: Time Aapke Pairon Mein Dheere Chalta Hai
topic: Gravitational time dilation: time runs slower at your feet than at your head, and GPS pays for it every day

payload.mechanism: the rate of a clock depends on gravitational potential, so height changes the rate of time
payload.number: about 1.1e-16 per metre; 470 nanoseconds between head and feet over 80 years; measured across one millimetre in 2022 (JILA, Nature); GPS clocks gain about 38 microseconds a day, which uncorrected is about 10 km of position per day
payload.consequence: there is no single 'now' - every height has its own, and every satellite fix is a relativity correction

retellTest: Aapka sar aapke pairon se tez chalta hai, aur GPS har roz thirty-eight microsecond ka hisaab karta hai - warna nakshey das kilometer khisak jaate.
sources: Bothwell et al., Nature 2022 - gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale strontium sample (JILA/NIST)
NIST press release, February 2022 - two clocks a millimetre apart tick at different rates
notes: One continuous camera move: base of the tower, up the wall, through the clock face, into the millimetre, out to orbit.
